title: Why blessings come first
hookLine: a book about farming opens with blessings: thank before you take
tomorrow: The corner of the field (Mishnah Peah)
last: A HARVEST IS NEVER ONLY YOURS.

lines: A FARMING BOOK THAT STARTS WITH THANKS.
cards: What should the first page of a farming law book talk about? Soil, maybe. When to plant.
How deep. The Mishnah's order of seeds does get to fields and furrows. But before anyone talks about corners or tithes or the seventh year, it opens with a book called Berakhot.
Blessings. Prayer at night and in the morning. Words to say before you bite into bread.
A farming book that starts with thank you. Today, why.

teach.b: Why blessings come first. Start with what's inside Berakhot. It opens with the Shema, the words said at night and in the morning.
Then the standing prayer. Then food: which blessing for the fruit of a tree, which for what grows from the ground, which for bread. Then it walks out of the house and into the world.

teach.h: LIGHTNING, MOUNTAINS, AND BAD NEWS TOO.
teach.b: On seeing lightning or hearing thunder, the Mishnah says, a person blesses the one whose strength and might fill the world. On mountains, seas and deserts, the one who makes the work of creation.

And a harder line: a person is to bless over bad news just as over good. So the first tractate is about a habit: meeting what comes with words of acknowledgment. Why put it at the head of the order about farms?
The Mishnah doesn't explain itself, so readers have offered answers. One runs like this: the order of seeds is about what you owe from your harvest, the corner, the tithes, the first fruits.

teach.h: BEFORE WHAT YOU OWE, WHOSE IT WAS.
teach.b: Before you learn what you owe, you learn whose it was to begin with. A companion work to the Mishnah, the Tosefta, puts the principle plainly: a person shouldn't taste anything without first saying a blessing.
Its reason is a line from the Psalms, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "The earth is the LORD'S, and the fulness thereof."
Thank before you take. In this way of seeing, the blessing isn't decoration on a meal. It's the first act of the harvest.

how: Jews say a blessing before eating and another after, and there are blessings for seeing lightning, mountains or the sea, for good news and for bad; the rules for all of them are set out in tractate Berakhot.

games.q: you're compiling a law book about farms. the chapters on corners, tithes and the seventh year are ready. what goes first?
o: blessings: thanks before anything is taken.
games.why: the order of seeds opens with Berakhot. before you learn what you owe from a harvest, you learn to thank for it.

practice: Set something you're about to eat or drink in front of you and don't touch it yet; just look at it, and let the small urge to reach for it wait.
Let your attention widen the way Berakhot walks out of the house: the light in the room, a sound outside.
Before the first bite, if you pray, say the blessing your tradition uses; if not, a plain thank you to whoever and whatever brought it.
